summary: If you’re looking for a modern Shooter experience that doesn’t take up much of your storage on your system, this is the game for you.
title: Battlefield 6
content:
Okay, I won’t lie, at first when I played this game, I was in awe of how this game is so good-looking for an initial 60GB game. Most games nowadays require a lot more storage and when I say a lot I truly mean it. Battlefield 6 holds up quite well for a game with that low storage.

## Visuals:

Visually, this game looks amazing. The atmosphere on almost every map feels astounding and don’t get me started on the destruction mechanics that are in the game. I remember starting out my first match and the first thing I did was throw a grenade to see if the building will get a bit destroyed and let me say I wasn’t too disappointed and I liked how basically most things in the game could be has that mechanic of being destroyed, it really captures the feeling of warfare. The Models of Guns in this game, well Detailed surprisingly,  cause sometimes I would look at the reloading animation and I be like:

> Damn, this s\*\** really looks good. They cooked.

Everything looks and feels smooth. Wow.



## Campaign:

Very Generic if I may say, a very boring campaign. It’s a boring story with no character depth, no personalities that really standout in this game and a whack progression from start to finish. In all honesty, I was just happy shooting at the AI, landing headshots and making evasive precautions. I also don’t like how the AI helps you a lot throughout this storyline. You could literally be a beginner playing on hardened and you would still complete a level. You have to be on your toes at all times, just running and gunning in order to have a bit of fun because the AI might kill all the opposition in your way. I would give the campaign a 4/10.

> And that’s me being nice to this game.

## \
Gameplay:

Man I could Run and Gun the whole day if there weren’t many players leaving this game (We’ll touch on that later). I feel like EA saw that they’re losing a lot in the shooter market and they felt like they had to make a decent game. Animations feel smooth. When I’m creeping around the corners to peek, it feels smooth. When I’m running and I want to slide, it feels smooth. When I want to dive into prone, it feels smooth. The recoil of guns make sense, depending on which weapon class you are using. There’s also crouch sprinting, which makes crouch movement a whole lot faster, and I mean a whole lot. There’s even different distances you could plan to shoot at when using a sniper rifle (which I’m yet to use in gameplay, I saw a YouTube video the other day explaining it). Every element that you can think of in a shooter experience is there and smooth. The only problem I have with the gameplay is the vehicle controls, but it’s not really that much of a train smash because it’s just one mechanic in a game that overall play and feels well.

## Additional Information:

If you’re playing the game a year later, you might struggle a bit with finding a decent online match as players are not really playing this game anymore, and it’s not because of the gameplay but the company that made the game. EA doesn’t want to listen to the game’s fanbase and in doing that, they are essentially losing the OG players attention (who make up around an estimate 85% of players from my calculations in my head). Don’t get me started on the Online progression, it is utterly draining and expects you to keep playing a lot of games in order to reach new ranks, I’d understand if it were the later ranks but now it’s the lower ranks which don’t even provide the effective guns in the game. I remember this other time playing at my boy’s place and said: 

> I’ve been grinding 3 hours for a scope on my boy’s console. Yea, I’m not doing this on mine.
verdict: If you’re looking for a Decent Shooter experience that is not Call of Duty, I’d suggest you to play Battlefield 6.
